Subject: Encryption & KMS options — follow-up from call

Hi Alex / Priya,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Quick recap from our discovery on encryption and key management, plus proposed next steps: 

What we heard
- PII in inference requests/outputs is a primary concern for AcmeHealth.
- You need clear controls for data retention and the ability to limit or redact logs.
- Desired data residency: US (primary) with future EU requirement.
- Preference for customer-managed keys (CMEK) and interest in HSM-backed key storage for sensitive workloads.

Redwood capabilities (high level)
- In-transit: TLS 1.2+ for all traffic; mutual TLS available for private deployments.
- At-rest: encrypted with AES-256; supports envelope encryption with customer-managed keys.
- KMS support: AWS KMS, GCP CMEK, Azure Key Vault, and integrations with partner HSMs for on-prem or dedicated deployments.
- Logs: request/response logging is configurable; we can redact PII and set retention windows per account.

Attachments I'm sharing: Redwood SOC2 summary, our encryption whitepaper, and a simple KMS architecture diagram (attachments below).

Proposed next steps
1) Tech review with our Solutions Engineer (Dev) to walk through CMEK flow and HSM options — proposed week of Nov 29.
2) Share SOC2 + architecture artifacts (attached).
3) Identify exact data residency requirements (region, backups) and whether you need EU-hosted data now or later.

Can you confirm whether Nov 30 or Dec 1 works for the tech review? Also, please confirm if AcmeHealth requires: (a) customer-managed keys for all environments, (b) HSM-backed keys, or (c) just KMS CMEK is sufficient for now.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Encryption & KMS options — follow-up from call

Alex — thanks, great questions. Answers below and next steps.

1) KMS compatibility
- Yes: Redwood supports AWS KMS and GCP CMEK with near-parity for key lifecycle operations (imported keys, rotation schedules, IAM-based access controls). For Azure we support Key Vault as well.
- When customers bring their own keys (CMEK), we use envelope encryption: customer master key in KMS protects a per-tenant data key that encrypts model artifacts and stored payloads. Redwood does not store or have access to the raw customer master key material.

2) Logs and PII
- Default logging: metadata only (timestamps, request id, model used, token counts). Request/response payloads are not stored in persistent logs by default for paid plans.
- Configurable options: you can enable full request logs for debugging, but these are opt-in and can be set to redact or hash specific fields (e.g., patient_id, ssn). We can also disable request payload logging entirely for regulated workloads.

3) Data retention
- Default transient logs retained for 30 days. Customers may set retention windows down to 0 days for no persistent log retention. For persisted inference outputs (e.g., if you opt to store generated content in your account), retention is configurable per account/route.

Attachments: I'm adding a slightly expanded KMS architecture diagram (kms-arch-diagram.png) and the SOC2 summary. If your security team needs the full SOC2 report or an NDA'd supplement, we can route that through our security team.

Tech review: Nov 30, 11:00 AM PST is confirmed. Dev will cover envelope encryption, CMEK flows for AWS/GCP, and HSM options. Calendar invite: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=tech-review-acme-20261130-1100

Next steps (action items)
- Marissa: Send expanded KMS diagram + SOC2 summary (attached) — DONE
- Dev: Technical walkthrough and sample IAM policy for CMEK usage — will present on Nov 30
- Acme: Confirm whether HSM-backed keys are required for production or if CMEK via cloud KMS suffices

If it helps, we can provision a private demo environment with CMEK enabled for your team to validate key access and audit logs ahead of any contract language.
